svg.title: The Scramble for Africa: Imperial Partition, Maxim Guns & Resistance (1879–1914)
svg.desc: KS3 Year 8 historical GIS atlas map of 1914 Colonial Africa and 1871–1914 Europe showing the 1884–85 Berlin Conference inside Imperial Germany, British rose Cape-to-Cairo and West African colonies, French blue colonies, King Leopold II’s amber Congo Free State, German/Portuguese/Italian/Spanish colonies, clearly marked independent Ethiopia (Abyssinia) and Liberia, and armed African resistance in Zululand (1879) and Matabeleland (1893).

text.tspan: carve up Africa with zero African leaders invited
drives an unbroken British corridor to the Cape
King Cetshwayo’s impis defeat British column
before heavy artillery & rifles crush Ulundi
BSAC Maxim guns defeat King Lobengula
by E. D. Morel & diplomat Roger Casement

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 8 ENQUIRY: THE SECOND BRITISH EMPIRE (1783–1914)
The Scramble for Africa: Partition, Maxim Guns & Resistance (1879–1914)
After the 1884–85 Berlin Conference, European empires used quinine and Maxim guns to seize 90% of Africa—leaving only Ethiopia and Liberia independent.
Behind “civilising mission” propaganda lay fierce African resistance in Zululand and Matabeleland and rubber-quota terror in Leopold II’s Congo.
